is_anopheles.evidence: The study screens wild-caught specimens of Nyssorhynchus darlingi (Anopheles darlingi) (page 1, Abstract; page 3, Section 2).

reports_target_markers.evidence: Target markers investigated include Vgsc codon 995 (L1014) and Ace-1 codon 280 (G119) (page 1, Abstract; page 5, Section 3.1; page 6, Section 3.2).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Genotype results are reported for 495 specimens for VGSC (all homozygous susceptible TTA / leucine at codon 995) and 493 specimens for Ace-1 (all homozygous susceptible GGG/GGG or GGG/GGC / glycine at codon 280), with sample sizes broken down by site in Table 1 (pages 4-6).

african_field_population.evidence: All mosquito collections were conducted in South America: three localities in Amazonian Peru (Gamitanacocha, Zungarococha, Cahuide) and four localities in Amazonian Brazil (Cruzeiro do Sul, Humaitá, Machadinho d'Oeste, Mâncio Lima) (page 1, Abstract; page 4, Table 1).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a primary research article performing molecular sequencing of field-collected mosquito specimens.

sub_country_location.evidence: Specific municipalities/villages with coordinates are provided in Table 1 (page 4), e.g., Cruzeiro do Sul, Acre, Brazil (-7.631889, -72.688722).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Most sites report specific collection years (e.g., 2015, 2016, 2018; Table 1, page 4).

duplicate_risk.evidence: Samples were collected as part of NIH-NIAID funded studies (ICEMR) and sequenced directly for this study.

supplement.evidence: All genotypic findings and sample numbers per site are fully described in the main manuscript text and Table 1.

assessment.summary: This study evaluated Ace-1 and VGSC target-site mutations in 495 Nyssorhynchus darlingi collected between 2014 and 2021 across seven localities in Amazonian Brazil and Peru. No resistance alleles were detected at Vgsc codon 995 or Ace-1 codon 280. The paper is ineligible because the mosquito populations are South American, not African.
